pictures.scene: Munkacsy, Christ before Pilate — Christ stands alone in a plain white robe in the middle of the governor's hall with His hands bound and His face lifted, while an accuser in a black mantle leans out over the crowd and levels a finger at Him, a soldier in a red cloak holds the people back with the shaft of his spear, and an old man in a red robe and a gold turban watches from the bench without moving, at that time some of those present told jesus about the galileans whose blood pilate had mixed with their sacrifices, …
pictures.name: pd_munkacsy_christ_before_pilate

pictures.scene: Beerstraaten, The Ruins of the Old Town Hall — a gutted stone tower still stands over a field of rubble with its wall torn open down one whole side, broken brickwork hanging loose, charred beams flung across the ground and the window frames burnt out, while a handful of small figures in dark cloaks pick their way along the foot of it, no, i tell you, but unless you repent, you too will all perish, or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of siloam collapsed on them, …
pictures.name: pd_beerstraaten_puinhopen_stadhuis

pictures.scene: Van Gogh, The Red Vineyard — the whole slope burns red and orange with vines turned by the autumn, and the pickers are bent along the rows in blue smocks and green aprons, stooping into the leaves and carrying the baskets down, while a wet track runs away through the middle of the vineyard, flashing with the colour of the sky above a low green hedge, then jesus told this parable, a man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard, …
pictures.name: pd_gogh_wijngaard

pictures.scene: Millet, Man with a Hoe — a labourer stops in the middle of the broken ground and leans his whole weight on the handle of his hoe, both scarred hands folded over the end of it, his white shirt hanging loose, his heavy trousers caked with earth and his face lifted with his mouth open to get his breath back, with the stones and clods of the half worked field spread out around his boots, so he said to the keeper of the vineyard, look, for the past three years i have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven't found any, …
pictures.name: pd_millet_man_with_a_hoe

pictures.scene: Gottlieb, Jews Praying in the Synagogue — the congregation is packed in under the stone vaulting on the day of atonement, men in striped prayer shawls bowed over the desks with their eyes shut and their hands pressed to their foreheads, one carrying the covered scroll in both arms down the crowded aisle, a boy in a bright coat standing at the front and the women leaning over the rail of the gallery above, one sabbath jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues, …
pictures.name: pd_gottlieb_jews_praying_on_yom_kippur

pictures.scene: Munkacsy, Woman Carrying Faggots — a woman has sat down on the bank at the edge of a dark wood with a great bundle of brushwood roped across her back, bent right forward under the weight of it with her arms folded over her knees, her head dropped and her face turned down, a red cap on her hair and a grey cloth padding her shoulder, and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years, she was hunched over and could not stand up straight, …
pictures.name: pd_munkacsy_vrouw_met_takkenbos

pictures.scene: Rembrandt, Simeon's Song of Praise — the old man kneels in the middle of the temple floor in a heavy gold embroidered robe with the child held up in both arms and his bearded face lifted into the light, blessing God aloud, while the young mother kneels beside him with her hands folded, a priest in a tall mitre stretches out his hand from the shadow and the whole dim temple rises away above them, then he placed his hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify god, …
pictures.name: pd_rembrandt_simeons_song_of_praise

pictures.scene: Berchem, Herdsmen Driving Cattle — the herd is being driven down the track in the warm evening light with a great horned ox swinging round at the front, a white backed cow and a dark cow crowding in behind him and the sheep pressing along the verge, while a herdsman in a broad hat walks ahead with his staff and a basket on his arm and a second man rides down after them on a donkey, with the hillside village and the hazy mountain standing above the road, you hypocrites, the lord replied, does not each of you on the sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water, …
pictures.name: pd_berchem_herders_met_vee

pictures.scene: Ryabushkin, A Moscow Street on a Holiday — the whole town is out in the wet street on the feast day and a young woman in a scarlet coat with a row of pearl buttons comes straight down the muddy planks with a taper held in both hands and a white embroidered kerchief over her hair, while a bearded man in a gold patterned coat and a tall black hat rides up behind her, two men rest against the painted icon shrine at the left, a black horse is led through the puddles and women in bright shawls stand at the timber houses beyond, when jesus said this, all his adversaries were humiliated, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things he was doing, …
pictures.name: pd_ryabushkin_moscow_street_holiday

pictures.scene: Bogdani, Birds in a Park — a great tree spreads over the corner of a garden and every branch and ledge of it is taken by birds, a parrot climbing the trunk high up, a finch and a blue tit out along a bough, a white fantail pigeon opening its wings on the carved urn with three more doves crowded beside it, a green parrot stooping to a cherry on the rim, a peacock trailing its whole tail down across the stone and a bullfinch and a canary picking about in the leaves at the bottom, it is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden, it grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches, …
pictures.name: pd_bogdani_vogels_in_een_park

pictures.scene: Artz, Grandmother — the old woman sits at the little round table in the dark cottage with a white cap over her grey hair and a white kerchief crossed at her throat, holding the brown loaf upright against the board with one hand and drawing the knife across it with the other, while a small fair child in a pinafore kneels up on a chair at the left with an empty plate and waits, and an older girl leans in at the right with a cup in her hand, it is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened, …
pictures.name: pd_artz_grootmoeder

pictures.scene: Bauernfeind, A Street in Jerusalem — the whole lane burns gold in the afternoon sun under a tall arched gateway thrown across it, with the crowd funnelling in and out of the narrow opening, an old man in a white headcloth coming down the cobbles on his stick, a boy in a red coat leading a dog past him, traders squatting in the shade of the stalls on the right and the jostle of turbans and striped robes packed away into the dim street beyond the arch, lord, someone asked him, will only a few people be saved, make every effort to enter through the narrow door, …
pictures.name: pd_bauernfeind_jerusalem_gate

pictures.scene: Holman Hunt, The Light of the World — Christ stands in the dark orchard at night in a white robe and a jewelled clasp with a gold crown of thorns on His head and a faint halo behind it, raising His hand to knock at a shut door buried in ivy and weeds that has not been opened for years, while He holds up a pierced lantern in His other hand so that its light falls out across the brambles, the fallen apples and the long grass about His bare feet, after the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, lord, open the door for us, …
pictures.name: pd_hunt_the_light_of_the_world

pictures.scene: Bendemann, The Mourning Jews in Exile — an old harper in a deep red robe and a yellow headcloth sits down on the ground under the vines with a chain hanging from the iron band on his wrist, his hand resting on the strings without playing, his bearded face turned away and his bare feet in the grass, while a young woman sinks down against his knee and buries her head in her arms, and he will answer, i tell you, i do not know where you are from, depart from me, all you evildoers, there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth, …
pictures.name: pd_bendemann_jews_mourning_in_exile

pictures.scene: Veronese, The Wedding at Cana — the long table is crowded right across the marble terrace with guests from every nation leaning in along it, Christ seated in the very middle in red and blue with a ring of light about His head and His mother beside Him in blue, turbaned men and bearded elders pressed in on both sides, a band of musicians playing lutes and viols at the front of the steps, servants carving and carrying dishes along the balustrade above and two hounds lying out on the chequered pavement below, people will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of god, …
pictures.name: pd_veronese_the_wedding_at_cana

pictures.scene: Cranach, The Stag Hunt of the Elector — the whole forest has been driven and the deer are being forced down off the wooded ridge into the bend of the river, swimming in a mass with their antlers above the water while the hounds go in after them, and along the near bank the princes stand among the bushes in plumed hats and dark velvet with their crossbows up and levelled, a huntsman in a red cap holding back the dogs at the corner and a dead stag lying across the sand at their feet, at that very hour, some pharisees came to jesus and told him, leave this place and get away, because herod wants to kill you, …
pictures.name: pd_cranach_the_stag_hunt_of_the_elector

pictures.scene: Hondecoeter, A Hen with Her Chicks — the white hen has dropped down onto the bare ground with her black tail feathers raised and her wings loosened out over the chicks, calling to them with her beak open while the little ones crowd in under her from both sides and one settles against her breast, and a great dark bird comes down out of the grey sky above her with its wings spread wide, o jerusalem, jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often i have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, …
pictures.name: pd_hondecoeter_hen_kuikens

pictures.scene: Church, Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives — the whole city lies along the far ridge in the late light behind its long wall with the great dome standing up in the middle of it and a tower of cloud climbing the sky above the roofs, while the dark valley of olive trees falls away empty between, and three small travellers with a laden camel have stopped on the stony track in the foreground and stand looking across at it, look, your house is left to you desolate, and i tell you that you will not see me again until you say, blessed is he who comes in the name of the lord, …
pictures.name: pd_church_jerusalem_from_the_mount_of_olives

lines.text: At that time some of those present told Jesus about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
To this He replied, Do you think that these Galileans were worse sinners than all the other Galileans, because they suffered this fate?
No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
Or those eighteen who were killed when the tower of Siloam collapsed on them: Do you think that they were more sinful than all the others living in Jerusalem?
No, I tell you. But unless you repent, you too will all perish.
Then Jesus told this parable: A man had a fig tree that was planted in his vineyard. He went to look for fruit on it, but did not find any.
So he said to the keeper of the vineyard, Look, for the past three years I have come to search for fruit on this fig tree and haven't found any. Therefore cut it down! Why should it use up the soil?
Sir, the man replied, leave it alone again this year, until I dig around it and fertilize it.
If it bears fruit next year, fine. But if not, you can cut it down.
One Sabbath Jesus was teaching in one of the synagogues,
and a woman there had been disabled by a spirit for eighteen years. She was hunched over and could not stand up straight.
When Jesus saw her, He called her over and said, Woman, you are set free from your disability.
Then He placed His hands on her, and immediately she straightened up and began to glorify God.
But the synagogue leader was indignant that Jesus had healed on the Sabbath. There are six days for work, he told the crowd. So come and be healed on those days and not on the Sabbath.
You hypocrites! the Lord replied. Does not each of you on the Sabbath untie his ox or donkey from the stall and lead it to water?
Then should not this daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has kept bound for eighteen long years, be released from her bondage on the Sabbath day?
When Jesus said this, all His adversaries were humiliated. And the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things He was doing.
Then Jesus asked, What is the kingdom of God like? To what can I compare it?
It is like a mustard seed that a man tossed into his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the air nested in its branches.
Again He asked, To what can I compare the kingdom of God?
It is like leaven that a woman took and mixed into three measures of flour, until all of it was leavened.
Then Jesus traveled throughout the towns and villages, teaching as He made His way toward Jerusalem.
Lord, someone asked Him, will only a few people be saved? Jesus answered,
Make every effort to enter through the narrow door. For many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
After the master of the house gets up and shuts the door, you will stand outside knocking and saying, Lord, open the door for us. But he will reply, I do not know where you are from.
Then you will say, We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.
And he will answer, I tell you, I do not know where you are from. Depart from me, all you evildoers.
There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, but you yourselves are thrown out.
People will come from east and west and north and south, and will recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
And indeed, some who are last will be first, and some who are first will be last.
At that very hour, some Pharisees came to Jesus and told Him, Leave this place and get away, because Herod wants to kill You.
But Jesus replied, Go tell that fox, Look, I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow, and on the third day I will reach My goal.
Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day, for it is not admissible for a prophet to perish outside of Jerusalem.

O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her, how often I have longed to gather your children together as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, but you were unwilling!
Look, your house is left to you desolate.
And I tell you that you will not see Me again until you say, Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord.
